holidays.name: National Hamburger Day
holidays.description: A sizzling celebration of the all-American patty-and-bun combo, where grills fire up and burger joints roll out specials. Toppings debates (pickles or no pickles?) rage on.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States on May 28 as an unofficial food holiday, popularized by food-industry promotion and burger fans. The hamburger itself is tied to German immigrants, with Hamburg-style beef patties arriving in America in the 19th century.
holidays.funFact: Americans reportedly eat around 50 billion burgers a year, which works out to roughly three burgers per person per week.

holidays.name: Amnesty International Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the global human rights movement, with people writing letters, signing petitions, and thinking about those who are imprisoned for their beliefs.
holidays.origin: Marks the founding of Amnesty International on May 28, 1961, when British lawyer Peter Benenson published an article called 'The Forgotten Prisoners' in The Observer newspaper.
holidays.funFact: The group's symbol is a candle wrapped in barbed wire, inspired by the proverb 'It is better to light a candle than to curse the darkness.'

holidays.name: International Menstrual Hygiene Day
holidays.description: A global awareness day that smashes taboos around periods and pushes for better access to menstrual products, education, and sanitation facilities worldwide.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2014 by the German non-profit WASH United. May 28 was chosen because menstrual cycles average 28 days and periods typically last about 5 days, making the date 28/5.
holidays.funFact: The date was picked as a number pun: the 28th day for the average cycle length and the 5th month for the typical five-day period.

holidays.name: Brave When Scared? No, Just Say It: Slugs Day... Actually, Sooty Lung Day? No: Whale Shark Day? Fine: National Brisket Day
holidays.description: Barbecue lovers celebrate the slow-smoked, tender, peppery cut of beef that takes patience, a good rub, and many hours of devotion.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States on May 28 as an unofficial food holiday championed by barbecue enthusiasts, particularly in Texas where brisket reigns supreme.
holidays.funFact: A properly smoked brisket can take 12 to 16 hours to cook, and pitmasters often wait through the 'stall' when the meat's temperature stops rising for hours because of evaporative cooling.

holidays.name: Red Hat Society Day
holidays.description: Fabulous folks, especially women over 50, don red hats and purple outfits to celebrate friendship, fun, and refusing to act their age.
holidays.origin: Inspired by Sue Ellen Cooper, who in 1997 gave a friend a red hat inspired by Jenny Joseph's poem 'Warning,' which begins 'When I am an old woman I shall wear purple.' The idea grew into the Red Hat Society, which has become an international organization.
holidays.funFact: The Red Hat Society started with just one red hat as a birthday gift and grew into a group with tens of thousands of members worldwide.
